newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso mixed but firmer at close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso mixed but firmer at close.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed mixed due to swap trades ahead of the weekend, but earlier weakness moderated at the close on Thursday, traders said.

"Some dealers stepped in to sell (dollars), who squared positions after key U.S. economic data were released...Peso returns looked attractive in the run up to the next major event," a trader said, referring to the Federal Open Market Committee meeting to review U.S. interest rates on May 20.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed unchanged at 7.8925/7.8960 per dollar, while its 24-hour stablemate ended 0.8 of a centavo firmer 7.8840/7.8850 per dollar.

Traders said the 48-hour contract peso recovered on late strength on the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond, which was up 6/32 to yield 6.87 when the foreign exchange market was closing in Mexico. The Dow Jones was meanwhile up 11.53 points at 7,297.69.
"To begin with, we were somewhat nervous over the Dow (Jones) and the (U.S. long) bond; nonetheless, when Wall Street recovered, the peso immediately picked up," another trader said.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 0.1 of a centavo firmer at 7.8840/7.8880 per dollar.
